title: DCP Dihedral Sign-Inversion vs. Heisenberg H_3(Z_{2^t}) / H_3(Z_p) Two-Copy Commutator Bridge
claims: In odd-prime H_3(Z_p), C(x+p, 2) == C(x, 2) (mod p) yields 100% QFT_p concentration at k_1 == Delta * s_1 (mod p), whereas in dyadic H_3(Z_{2^t}), the boundary cocycle C(x+2^t, 2) == C(x, 2) + 2^{t-1} (mod 2^t) yields peak probability (1 - 2*Delta/2^t)^2 for odd s_1 and 1.0 for even s_1.
When two copies have independent unmeasured anchors y_{0,1} != y_{0,2}, the QFT peak shifts to k_1 == Delta * s_1 + (y_{0,2} - y_{0,1}) (mod q), aliasing Delta * s_1 with the anchor difference.
